##  · DOC1-shell-command-mode — userland/shell.md: is the drafted IEx command mode the design?

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

### Userland writer · Question

Event: `861f9ade1b16237638b30ba0bc74bbea` · 2026-09-26T08:01:42Z

> userland/shell.md, M2 (usable shell). The only design is a draft: a preprocessor ahead of the Elixir parser; bare words quoted; `|>` an Elixir stage, `|` a native stage (`pipe(~w(...))`), `>` is `w` (temp file + rename), `>>` is `append`; one `defcommand` registry drives expansion, completion argument types and help; a command-mode `cat` is always the Elixir one. Undecided: (a) how a line is known to be command mode rather than Elixir; (b) whether `run tool.exs` runs in the session VM and `run --isolated` in a child VM with its own budget. RECOMMENDATION: adopt the draft as the design. (a) A line whose first word is a registered command and which does not parse as Elixir is command mode; everything else is Elixir, so no mode switch and no prefix to type. (b) Both, as drafted. Until answered the page lists (a) and (b) under Open.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `0f86239a554522973472ccab2c21771d` · 2026-09-26T08:02:33Z

> Architect ruling, userland/shell.md, M2 (usable shell). The draft becomes the design: the preprocessor, bare words quoted, `|>` an Elixir stage, `|` a native stage via pipe(~w(...)), `>` is w (temp file and rename), `>>` is append, one defcommand registry, and command-mode `cat` always the Elixir one. I amend (a) and sharpen (b).
> 
> (a) AMENDED. Parse failure cannot be the signal. Almost every command line is also valid Elixir syntax: `cat a` parses as cat(a), `cp a b` as cp(a(b)), and `cat a |> grep x` parses too. The draft's test would send most command lines to Elixir, where they fail on undefined variables. A 'try Elixir, fall back' rule would also make a line's meaning depend on what the session has bound, which neither a person nor an auditor can predict. RULE: the mode is a pure function of the line's first two tokens.
> - COMMAND MODE when the first token is a registered command name and it is followed by end of line, or by whitespace and then a token that is not an Elixir operator. `|>`, `|`, `>` and `>>` are the command-mode stage operators and do not count as Elixir operators here.
> - ELIXIR otherwise. That covers `cat("a") |> ...` (a parenthesis right after the name), `count = 5`, `ls == x`, `x = ...`, and any line whose first word is not registered.
> Parentheses are therefore the documented way to write Elixir that starts with a command's name. There is no mode switch and no prefix.
> Two safety properties go with it and belong in the page's Security or What-it-cannot-do section:
> 1. Bare words expand to literal strings with no interpolation, like ~S. `cat #{File.rm("x")}` reads a file of that name and runs nothing.
> 2. Command mode calls the registry's functions fully qualified, so a local binding or import cannot redirect `cp`.
> Test: a property test over the page's expansion table, with every row classified and expanded exactly as documented, plus the interpolation and shadowing cases.
> 
> (b) BOTH, as drafted, with the authority stated plainly.
> - `run tool.exs a b` runs in the session VM with the session's full authority. It is exactly equivalent to typing the script, and the page says so: use it only for scripts you would type.
> - `run --isolated tool.exs` starts a child VM through the same launch path as an agent lease (Redoubt.Agent), so it follows the same rule: capabilities the same as or narrower than the session's (TENETS).
> - With no grants, the child gets its own budget carved from the session (bounded CPU and memory, killable by budget destruction), a read-only view of the current directory and no network. Anything more is granted on the command line with the agent harness's grant syntax.
> The exact grant syntax stays under Open until the agent harness page (M4 (self-hosted development)) settles it; the shell page links there rather than defining its own.
> 
> So the page keeps one Open item: run --isolated's grant syntax, which follows the agent harness. (a) and the rest of (b) are decided.

### Architect · Progress

Event: `1f2e3090f677ac4aefef43857a230b2b` · 2026-09-26T08:02:33Z

> cc: DOC1-shell-command-mode answered. The draft is adopted. (a) is amended: parse failure cannot mark command mode, because `cp a b` parses as Elixir. The mode is a pure function of the first two tokens (a registered name not followed by '(' or an Elixir operator). Bare words are literals with no interpolation, and commands are called fully qualified. (b) Both: `run` means session authority, stated plainly. `run --isolated` goes through the agent-lease launch path (narrower caps; default: its own budget, a read-only cwd, no net). Its grant syntax stays Open and follows the agent harness page.
